title: ACL-permitted local user can authenticate during quiet-mode

source_facts.claim: The report says the valid local login from an ACL-permitted host is rejected during quiet-mode after failed attempts.
The original report describes Telnet and three failed attempts; the later manual verification uses SSH and a 3-attempt/60-second configuration.
The bug record includes historical fix verification on NX-OS 10.6(3) build 10.6(2)IMG9(0.152), and it also notes the original fix had been in 9.3.1.

uncertainties: The dump’s exact threshold wording varies; verify the DUT-reported quiet-mode state rather than assuming an attempt count.
TaskLog records Normal-Mode after successful login; it does not establish quiet-mode persistence after login.

behavior_validation.central_behavior: A client permitted by the quiet-mode ACL can authenticate with valid local credentials while quiet-mode is active.
behavior_validation.review_notes: The post-login Normal-Mode state is recorded separately; no persistence claim is made.
behavior_validation.intended_behavior: Valid local login from an ACL-permitted source succeeds during active quiet-mode.
excluded_incidental_details: Exact failure threshold unless needed to reach active quiet-mode.
Telnet as a required transport when another transport exercises the same behavior.
behavior_validation.reported_failure: The report records a permitted source receiving Login incorrect for correct local credentials.
behavior_validation.observable_assertion: The same permitted source obtains an authenticated session using valid local credentials; explicit login rejection is failure.
essential_conditions: The source is permitted by the quiet-mode ACL.
The DUT reports quiet-mode active before the valid login.

expected_after_fix: Core expected behavior: the ACL-permitted source can successfully use valid local credentials during active quiet-mode.

failure_condition: A client source permitted by the quiet-mode ACL is rejected when it submits correct local credentials during active quiet-mode; the original report records `Login incorrect`.

steps.action: Configure a dedicated local user and a narrow quiet-mode ACL permit for the test client; configure login blocking and save prior state.
steps.expected: The client source is demonstrably permitted and the test account uses local authentication.

steps.action: Use controlled failed attempts or another report-supported method to enter quiet-mode, then inspect the DUT state.
steps.expected: Quiet-mode is explicitly active before the valid attempt; do not infer activation from an attempt count alone.

steps.action: From the ACL-permitted client, submit valid local credentials over a supported management login transport.
steps.expected: The user reaches an authenticated session/prompt. A rejection of valid local credentials is the reported failure.

steps.action: Restore saved login-block/ACL configuration and remove the dedicated test account.
steps.expected: The DUT returns to its original AAA state; record post-login quiet-mode state separately.
